population.note: FICTIONAL. Ever-users minus current users: 34.5 − 25.4 = 9.1% of adults have used and are now off. The 8.0 points of new ever-users since 2030 split into 6.4 on and 1.6 already off. Of the 26.5 points who had used by 2030, 19.0 are on and 7.5 are off. Within that 2030 cohort, 10.5 of the 18.8 then on stayed on (56% persistence over two years). The other 8.3 stopped and joined the 7.7 already off, a pool of 16.0, of whom 8.5 restarted (53% over two years, in line with the parent's 55%). So 10.5 + 8.5 = 19.0 on and 16.0 − 8.5 = 7.5 off. Totals: on 6.4 + 19.0 = 25.4, off 1.6 + 7.5 = 9.1. Cycled: the 8.9 points who had cycled by 2030, plus about 3.1 points of first-time restarters in the pool and 0.3 among new starters, gives 12.3 of 34.5 = 36%. About 68.6M of ~270M adults are current users. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 2.8 + 9.24 + 9.6 + 3.8 = 25.4. Income thirds: (31 + 25 + 20.2)/3 = 25.4. The bottom third rose most, by 7.2 points, through HRSA free provision, Medicaid, cessation coverage (smoking is concentrated in lower incomes), enlisted military programmes and the gray market. The middle third rose 6.5 points despite the employer retreat, mostly by moving to cash portals, cessation and AUD coding, and compounded pens. The top third rose 6 points. The 50–64 band is at 40%, the first band where users are near-majority among people with obesity. The 65+ band rose more slowly (12 → 16.5) after the NAION class label, because ophthalmology history now screens some people out. Off-drug: ~24.6M adults used and stopped, and ~177M never used. The never-used are now treated as a group that needs explaining: pregnant or trying to conceive, NAION or eye history, aircrew in an initiation window, people who declined on principle, and the uninsured middle-income who will not pay $349–449. Pediatric: 1.1% of ~73M ≈ 800k, of whom ≈150k are aged 6–11 (liraglutide). First interim registry bone data were reported in 2032.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was renewed again in Dec 2031, through 2033, at the unchanged $275/month payment and $50 copay. About 3.0M use it for obesity: 3.0M × $275 × 12 ≈ $9.9B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈14.6% of fills ≈ 10.0M users (≈9.5M aged 65+ and 0.5M disabled). Medicaid pays ≈12% ≈ 8.2M users at $275: 8.2M × $275 × 12 ≈ $27.1B/yr combined federal and state, driven by expansion-state cessation coverage. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program: FY2031 $5.0B and FY2032 $5.9B. It serves 2.4M on liraglutide (2.4M × $85 × 12 = $2.45B) and 1.4M on cessation/AUD semaglutide (1.4M × $199 × 12 = $3.34B), ≈ $5.8B for 3.8M users. Federal workforce channel ≈2.0% ≈ 1.4M users: VA ≈0.9M (AUD, weight, diabetes) and TRICARE/DHA ≈0.5M. Within TRICARE, the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program covers ≈270k active-duty and reserve members at a DLA contract of ~$230/month: 270k × $230 × 12 ≈ $0.75B/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India sells 80+ semaglutide brands at $7–40/month, and the first generic tirzepatide launched there in 2032 at $30–70. Generic semaglutide is sold in Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey, China and most of the EU's neighbours, and generic oral semaglutide in ~180 countries. In the US, Paragraph IV settlements (Dec 2031) set first generic semaglutide entry at Q2 2033, and tirzepatide exclusivity runs to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~68.6M users: commercial 30.0% (20.6M), Medicare 14.6% (10.0M), Medicaid 12.0% (8.2M), HRSA free provision 5.5% (3.8M), VA/TRICARE 2.0% (1.4M), cash/direct 17.4% (11.9M), gray market 18.5% (12.7M), totalling 100% and 68.6M. Prices stalled for a fourth year. TrumpRx/direct cash is still $349 for semaglutide, $449 for tirzepatide and $199 for oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo). Wegovy lists at $1,349 and retatrutide at $1,499, still allocated. Section 232 tariffs are unchanged, and the generic-entry settlement removed the expectation of a 2032 price break. Employer retreat: weight-management coverage fell from 57% to 45%. The largest PBMs now sell 'indication-coded' formularies that pay only on T2D, established CVD, OSA, CKD, MASH, cessation (ACA mandate, 2×90-day courses) and AUD (parity). Commercial users still rose from 17.8M to 20.6M, entirely through coded indications, while weight-only commercial fills fell by roughly a third. People the employers dropped moved to cash (7.0M → 11.9M) and to gray product (9.0M → 12.7M). Gray prices are unchanged: 503A 'personalised' semaglutide $129–249, Indian mail pens $7–40 plus shipping, research retatrutide $120–250.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029)
nicotine dependence incl. e-cigarette/vaping cessation, adults (orforglipron/Foundayo, Feb 2032; semaglutide cessation label broadened to all nicotine products, Nov 2031)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health'/longevity regimens with DEXA and strength coaching, top income third
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology
vaping cessation in 16–17-year-olds (Foundayo), prescribed by adolescent-medicine clinics
'calm' and 'focus' low-dose subscriptions, shrinking after the 2031 label change and FTC consent orders (~0.8M users, down from 1.5–2M)
research-peptide retatrutide for 'recomposition' and pre-competition 'cuts' in gyms
gambling and cannabis reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached the US market (driver: none). MariTide (monthly; BLA filed Jul 2030) received a CRL in Jun 2031 asking for more titration and GI-tolerability data and a dedicated BMD substudy. It has been resubmitted, with a decision expected in 2033. Survodutide was approved in the EU for MASH in 2031; its US resubmission went to an advisory committee that split 7–6 on the hepatic signal in Apr 2032, and the FDA extended review into 2033. Amycretin was resubmitted after Novo's facility reinspection, with a decision expected in 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3. The nicotine driver came through as supplements to existing drugs: orforglipron was approved for smoking and vaping cessation in Feb 2032, and semaglutide's cessation label was broadened in Nov 2031. The incretin market is ≈$170B in 2032. US volume rose about 37% at stalled net prices, and ex-US generic erosion accelerated.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Orforglipron cessation users report GI-driven early stops in the first 4 weeks at rates similar to semaglutide.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established. Persistence after discontinuation is still disputed. MDL 3094 passed ~58,000 filed and tolled claims. The second bellwether (Oct 2031) was a defence verdict. Settlement talks have opened but are unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis. Reserves increased.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss, and rising in absolute numbers with volume and research-peptide use.
Still no causal confirmation and a low absolute risk. About 8,000 claims sit inside the MDL.

Still a population problem in 65+, concentrated in unmonitored, low-efficacy and low-protein users. The DoD programme pairs drug with mandatory strength training, and early data show lean-mass preservation in that group.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The 2028 class label stands, and the Bridge counselling visit is retained. HRSA added optional grip-strength screening in 2032, which is not required.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term and cycling users, concentrated in women. Interim pediatric registry data (2032, n≈4,100) show slightly lower BMD z-score gains in 6–11-year-olds versus matched controls. The finding is not yet interpreted because weight loss confounds it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended in 65+ and postmenopausal women. FDA requested a second pediatric bone analysis and made no label change yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A pooled Medicare–VA–Nordic cohort (2031) found HR ≈1.9 (95% CI 1.5–2.4) with consistent class-wide dose–response, highest in people with diabetes and crowded optic discs. The excess risk is roughly 3–6 per 100,000 person-years in non-diabetic users. Across ~68M users that implies an estimated 2,000–4,000 additional cases a year. About 3,500 NAION claims have been added to the MDL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class warning in Warnings & Precautions for all GLP-1 receptor agonists (Aug 2031), moving the risk from 'very rare' to a labelled class risk. Labels advise baseline eye history and stopping the drug if sudden vision loss occurs. FAA and the DoD require baseline and annual OCT for aircrew on incretins. EMA aligned in 2032.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The retatrutide postmarketing study, released in full after the Lilly disclosure scandal, found clinically significant anhedonia (validated-scale threshold) in 1.8% of the 12 mg arm versus 0.6% on placebo, dose-dependent. Class rates are lower for semaglutide and tirzepatide. Milder self-reported reduced pleasure persists at ~10–15% of long-term users, and the label does not count it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Oct 2031: 'anhedonia/emotional blunting' added as an uncommon adverse reaction for retatrutide, with class language in Adverse Reactions for the others. FTC consent orders with six 'focus' telehealth brands. HELP and DOJ inquiries into Lilly are ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Driven increasingly by structural stops. Employers dropped weight coverage in Jan 2031 and Jan 2032, the 2×90-day cessation cap applies, and some aircrew and drivers stop at NAION screening.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D and protein signals persist in older and low-income users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult and nine of adolescent follow-up. About 150k children aged 6–11 are on drug. Pubertal-timing data are still pending.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry ongoing; second bone analysis requested.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls rose a further ~40% from 2030 to 2032 as gray users grew to ~12.7M. Clusters of NAION-like and dosing-error presentations are reported among research-retatrutide users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters and import alerts continue. The first federal criminal case (2032) targets a peptide distributor, not individual users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; higher in research-peptide users.

food_and_beverage.state: With a quarter of adults on drug and 40% of 50–64s, US snack, confectionery and sugary-drink volumes keep falling, at a rate similar to 2028–30 rather than accelerating, because new users are lower-dose and cycling. Two majors completed indulgent-brand divestitures. 'Coded-diet' lines (protein, fibre, bone and 'quit-friendly' oral-fixation snacks such as gum, seeds and jerky) keep growing. Discount grocers in military towns stock DoD-programme protein packs.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volumes fall again as AUD coverage, VA adoption and the normalised 'I'm on it' excuse at the bar spread. Non-alcoholic and premium single-pour formats grow. Tobacco is hit harder: Foundayo's vaping label and quitline provision push cigarette and vape volumes down sharply, and state budgets in Kentucky, Ohio and Texas cut tobacco excise forecasts.

restaurants.state: Value-volume chains and buffets keep closing suburban units, and alcohol attach rates keep falling. Half-portion menus are standard. Fast-casual protein bowls and small-plate dining are steady.

apparel.state: Size runs keep moving down at the median. 'Athletic-cut' tailoring is still the growth segment. Military exchange stores report record uniform re-issue volume as service members change sizes. Plus-size retail is shrinking but has stabilised among the uninsured middle.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios keep expanding, and municipal and police wellness contracts become a new revenue line. The DoD programme's mandatory strength component has created a contractor market around bases. Research-peptide sales in gyms persist.

insurance.state: Employers retreat: weight-management coverage is down from 57% to 45%, and indication-coded formularies are the PBM product of the year. Commercial pharmacy trend cools to ~+7% as weight-only fills fall, but coded fills rise. Cost shifts to employees paying $349–449 cash. Some plans add NAION eye-screening requirements as a prior-auth step.

pharma.state: Lilly is still the volume leader, but its stock fell ~18% on the retatrutide disclosure scandal, and it faces a DOJ civil investigative demand and HELP hearings. Novo has stabilised after reinspection and won a generic-entry settlement that holds semaglutide prices into 2033. Stalled prices plus volume make for record US revenue. Indian generic makers are positioned for 2033 US entry.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug no longer signals anything. Being off now needs an explanation: 'trying for a baby', 'off for my eyes', 'pilot medical', 'my plan dropped it', or 'I just don't want to'. The quality of the result still signals class: muscle and bone versus thinness without much muscle. In San Antonio, the uniform carries a third signal: the lean, trained body from the DoD readiness programme, which reads as enlisted and state-issued.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The middle third is where the class line shows. People who lost employer coverage in 2031–32 are visibly regaining weight or have moved to compounded pens. In San Antonio, an enlisted airman on programme semaglutide and a strength mandate can look fitter than the civilian contractor beside him who pays $449 cash or has stopped. People say 'you can tell whose plan dropped it'.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Half portions are the default at restaurants and family tables. Thanksgiving is planned around dose day. Quitting nicotine has its own rituals: gum bowls at offices and sunflower seeds on base. The cigarette break is gone from many workplaces, replaced by the walk.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles rarely state on or off any more because on is assumed. 'Off' is now the disclosure, and it often signals pregnancy plans or a health reason. Couples with mismatched appetites are common enough that therapists treat it as routine.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a clinical variable. Nicotine craving has joined alcohol and food as something you get a prescription for. Normalisation has quieted the moral reading. A craving is now less a choice than a lapse in coverage.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The label now gives a number: clinically significant anhedonia in 1.8% on high-dose retatrutide versus 0.6% on placebo, lower for the other agents, listed as 'uncommon'. The 10–15% of long-term users who report milder reduced pleasure are not counted. Clinicians call it 'subthreshold' and adjust the dose. 'Focus' subscriptions fell from 1.5–2M to ~0.8M users after the label change and FTC consent orders.
interior_life.framing: An uncommon side effect, recognised in clinics. Primary care and quitline intake forms include a two-item anhedonia screen. 'The grey' survives as slang, but marketing it as a feature is legally risky now that it appears on the label as a harm.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Most finance and logistics employers dropped 'focus' perks in 2032 after counsel warned that subsidising a labelled adverse effect created liability. DoD readiness programme intake includes PHQ and anhedonia screening, and drill instructors joke about 'the calm platoon'. Sales staff still dose down before quarter-end.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'off-dose' music and comedy circuit lost some novelty now that the effect is officially small. A few performers who used anhedonia as a selling point now file claims instead. Sports-betting handle stays soft in high-uptake states. Leisure keeps shifting toward short, intense experiences.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose as a matter of course. Some couples now call a partner's flatness a side effect worth reporting rather than a personality trait.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Lilly scandal gives 2032 candidates a pharma-accountability line. Price stalls and employer retreat are kitchen-table issues in the middle third. Nobody asks candidates whether they are 'on' any more; reporters ask why the one who isn't has stopped.

state.regulatory_posture: The regulator is now willing to tighten labels it had resisted: an NAION class warning, anhedonia listed as an uncommon adverse reaction, and a MariTide CRL. Supplemental indications are still approved quickly (Foundayo for vaping). The FDA and FTC jointly police wellness claims. DOJ is investigating Lilly's handling of postmarketing data.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: HRSA programme renewed at $5.9B for FY2032. Medicare Bridge renewed through 2033 at $275/$50. The ACA cessation mandate now covers Foundayo. FY2031 NDAA authorises the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program. Texas, Florida and Georgia fund first-responder metabolic health grants for police, corrections and fire departments. Nobody is mandated to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged. Under the DoD programme, members who fail body-composition standards are offered the drug with mandatory strength training. Declining is not punishable, but failing standards still is. Commanders see only duty-limiting status, not adherence. Aircrew are grounded (DNIF) for the first 30 days after starting and need annual OCT.
state.workforce_or_military: The drug is now readiness infrastructure. About 270k active-duty and reserve members are on it, the Army keeps its recruit policy, and the VA treats AUD with it. FAA medical policy allows semaglutide and tirzepatide for pilots after an observation period, with NAION screening added in 2031. DOT apnea clearance still effectively requires tirzepatide for some drivers. State police programmes are concentrated in Texas.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs are unchanged. Indian generic tirzepatide (2032) widens the mail-order gray supply. DLA contracting for the DoD programme favours US-filled semaglutide, which gives Novo's reinspected North Carolina site a strategic constituency. Indian API is still the main input for 503A compounding.

events.event: Pentagon launches the Metabolic Readiness Program under the FY2031 NDAA, offering semaglutide or tirzepatide with mandatory strength training to service members failing body-composition standards; Air Force sets 30-day grounding window for aircrew starting treatment

Internal documents published by a former CRO statistician show Eli Lilly re-specified the primary endpoint and delayed the readout of its retatrutide postmarketing anhedonia study after unfavourable interim data; HELP Committee subpoenas records, DOJ opens a civil investigation, and full results released in September show 1.8% clinically significant anhedonia at top dose versus 0.6% placebo; FDA adds it as an uncommon adverse reaction in October

FDA requires a class warning for NAION across all GLP-1 receptor agonists after a pooled Medicare–VA–Nordic cohort finds roughly doubled risk; FAA and DoD add baseline and annual optical coherence tomography for aircrew on incretins

Novo Nordisk settles Paragraph IV litigation with generic semaglutide filers, setting first US generic entry for Q2 2033; TrumpRx cash prices held at $349/$449/$199 for a fourth year and Section 232 tariff unchanged

Employer benefit surveys show weight-management coverage down to 45% for the 2032 plan year as the three largest PBMs roll out 'indication-coded' formularies paying only for diabetes, cardiac, apnea, kidney, liver, cessation and alcohol-use codes
FDA approves orforglipron (Foundayo) for smoking and vaping cessation in adults, bringing a $199 oral option under the ACA preventive mandate and state quitlines

open_tensions: Employers have retreated and prices have stalled, so middle-income Americans keep their drug by paying $349–449 cash, buying compounded pens, or getting coded for cessation or alcohol use. The Q2 2033 generic semaglutide entry could collapse cash prices or be delayed again, and the PBMs' coded formularies are built for either outcome.

The drug is now readiness infrastructure for soldiers, pilots and police just as an NAION class warning makes eye screening a duty-fitness question. The first aircrew vision-loss case in the programme would test both the DoD and the FAA.

The Lilly scandal turned reward blunting into a measured, labelled, uncommon harm. That smaller official number sits awkwardly beside the 10–15% who say they feel less, the DOJ inquiry, and new anhedonia claims arriving in an MDL that already holds ~58,000 claims.

About 150k children aged 6–11 are on liraglutide, normalisation makes the drug unremarkable at the family table, and the first interim registry data show slightly lower bone gains that nobody has yet interpreted.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 a month, is supply-allocated, has no TrumpRx cash price, and carries its bone and body-composition monitoring section.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: One in Four: In 2032 Nobody Asks If You're On It. They Ask Why You Stopped.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about sixty-eight million American adults, one in four, take an incretin drug, and almost nobody comments on it any more. Among people aged fifty to sixty-four the figure is forty percent. At work, at the bar and on a first date, the person who has to explain is the one who isn't on it. They are usually pregnant or trying, or they have a history in one eye, or they are a pilot waiting out a medical, or their plan dropped it in January.

Plans did drop it. Prices stopped falling and did not start again. The cash portal still charges $349 a month for semaglutide, $449 for tirzepatide and $199 for the starter pills. In December 2031 Novo Nordisk settled its patent fight with the generic makers and set the first American generic for the spring of 2033. Employers decided they would not keep carrying open-ended weight coverage while waiting for it. Fewer than half still pay for weight loss alone. The largest benefits managers now sell formularies that pay only for a diagnosis code: diabetes, heart disease, apnea, kidney, liver, quitting or drinking less. Commercial users went up anyway, because the codes kept coming. The people who had no code went to the cash portal or to a compounded pen. About thirteen million Americans now use product no regulator has inspected.

Nicotine is the newest code. In February the FDA approved Lilly's daily pill, Foundayo, for quitting cigarettes and vapes. Under the preventive mandate every plan must cover two ninety-day courses a year, and state quitlines hand it out free. Vape shops near high schools are closing, Kentucky has cut its excise forecast, and break rooms smell of sunflower seeds.

The drug is also now readiness infrastructure. Since January 2031 the Pentagon's Metabolic Readiness Program has offered semaglutide or tirzepatide, along with a mandatory strength programme, to service members who fail body-composition standards. About 270,000 are enrolled. Texas pays for it for state troopers and corrections officers. In San Antonio, which has more uniforms than anywhere else, the trained, state-issued body of an enlisted airman often looks better than that of the civilian contractor beside him who pays cash or quit when his plan changed.

In August 2031 the eyes became a problem. A pooled cohort of Medicare, VA and Nordic patients found that the risk of NAION, a sudden stroke of the optic nerve, roughly doubles on these drugs. The absolute risk is small, but at this volume it means a few thousand additional cases a year. The FDA moved it from a footnote to a class warning. Aircrew now get scanned before they start and every year after. Eye clinics in base towns are booked out for months. Some pilots chose to stop.

The scandal came from Lilly. A former contractor statistician published documents showing that the company had changed the endpoint and delayed the readout of its retatrutide study on pleasure and mood after the early numbers looked bad. When the full data came out, they showed clinically significant anhedonia in fewer than two percent of people on the top dose. That is a real effect and an uncommon one, and it is now printed on the label. The 'focus' subscriptions that sold quiet as a product mostly shut down, and employers stopped paying for them because their lawyers would not let them subsidise a listed harm. Clinics now ask two questions about joy at intake. The one in eight long-term users who say they feel a little less are told they are subthreshold.

The lawsuits keep growing, with about fifty-eight thousand claims in Philadelphia. The second bellwether went to the defence. About 150,000 children under twelve take liraglutide, and the first bone data are slightly low, with no explanation yet. The country looks leaner and calmer, and it drinks and smokes less. You can no longer tell who is on the drug. You can still tell who is paying for it.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rosa Villarreal's alarm goes at 5:10. The Foundayo pill is next to the coffee maker, where the vape used to charge. It is day sixty-one of her second course. Her app counts down: twenty-nine covered days left this year.

Arturo is already in uniform, shaking his pen like a paint can. Tuesday is his shot. Thursday is the eye scan at Wilford Hall, because his squadron moved him to flight-line duty. "They'll look at the back of my eyeball," he says, "and I'll look at the ceiling."

At the hangar at Port San Antonio, Benny from avionics has gained back his face. He doesn't wait to be asked. "Plan dropped it. Not paying four-fifty." Someone mentions a site that ships from Hyderabad. Benny says his cousin's eye went dark for a week and leaves it there.

At lunch Rosa eats half a brisket taco and wraps the other half for her son. Nobody at the table finishes theirs. A woman from purchasing says she's off because she's trying for a baby, and everyone says congratulations instead of asking.

At 3:40 her phone buzzes: Quit Coach, two questions. In the past two weeks, have you had little interest or pleasure in doing things? She thinks about it longer than she means to and taps Several days.

At home Mateo, fifteen, is at the counter eating the taco. "Dani's on the liraglutide now," he says. "From the clinic. It's free."

"Dani's eleven."

"So?"

Arturo comes in and kisses her and tastes the seeds she's been chewing all day. On the patio, out of habit, she reaches for the pocket where the vape used to be. Her hand finds nothing there, and she leaves it in her pocket anyway.
